artists.biography:
The Sisters of Mercy are an English rock band, formed in 1980 in Leeds. After achieving early underground fame there, the band had their commercial breakthrough in the mid-1980s and sustained it until the early 1990s, when they stopped releasing new recorded output in protest against their record company WEA. Currently, the band are a touring outfit only.

The group has released three original studio albums: First and Last and Always (1985), Floodland (1987) and Vision Thing (1990). Each album was recorded by a different line-up; singer-songwriter Andrew Eldritch and the drum machine called Doktor Avalanche are the only points of continuity throughout. Eldritch and Avalanche were also involved in The Sisterhood, a side-project connected with Eldritch's dispute with former members.

The Sisters of Mercy ceased recording activity in the early 1990s, when they went on strike against East West Records, whom they accused of incompetence and withholding royalties, and had pressured the group to release at least two more studio albums; instead, the label released the album Go Figure under the moniker SSV in 1997. Although the Sisters of Mercy were eventually released from their contract with East West, they have never been signed to another label nor released any new material, despite showcasing numerous new songs in their live sets.

Former members of the group established the bands Ghost Dance and The Mission.

perplexity.description:
Greatest Hits Volume One - A Slight Case Of Overbombing" is a 1993 compilation album by The Sisters of Mercy, released on their own Merciful Release label in partnership with Warner Music Group. The album collects the band's most significant tracks in reverse chronological order, showcasing their evolution within the rock and gothic rock genres. It includes key songs such as "Under The Gun," the 1992 version of "Temple Of Love" featuring Ofra Haza, and other notable hits like "This Corrosion" and "Lucretia My Reflection".

Musically, the album highlights The Sisters of Mercy's signature blend of dark, atmospheric rock characterized by driving drum machines, deep baritone vocals by Andrew Eldritch, and layered guitar textures. This compilation serves as a comprehensive overview of their influential sound that helped define gothic rock in the 1980s and early 1990s. Critically, it was well-received as a definitive collection of the band's work up to that point, consolidating their status in the alternative rock scene. Commercially, it supported the band's 1993 "Overbombing" tour, primarily in Europe, further cementing their legacy.

Positioned in the band's discography, "A Slight Case Of Overbombing" functions as a summation of their output before a long hiatus from releasing new studio albums. It captures the peak of their creative period and remains an essential entry for fans and newcomers seeking a thorough introduction to The Sisters of Mercy's influential style and catalog.
